CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zucsv reads CSV files into data frames. read_csv() in R/read_csv.R is a thin wrapper over the C reader in src/read_csv.c and src/convert.c, built on the vendored parser under src/vendor/zsv/. Base R C API only, no runtime R package dependencies.

The full design document is .agents/zucsv-design.md and the staged plan is .agents/ROADMAP.md. Both are build-ignored (^\.agents$), so they stay out of the tarball. They outrank this file.

Read .agents/zucsv-design.md before writing any code. It is the specification for v0.1 and covers the public API, type-inference rules, error messages, two-pass strategy, resource limits, the src/ file layout, and the explicit non-goals. Treat its “Non-goals for v0.1” (§3) as binding: do not add write_csv(), connections, URL input, date parsing, column selection, skip/n_max, ALTREP, or a parser-mode switch unless the user asks to revise the design. They still bind after 0.1.0, until a design revision lifts one. §29 is the decision log; check it before reopening a choice that looks arbitrary. .agents/ROADMAP.md says which stage the work is in and what its exit criteria are; finish a stage’s criteria before starting the next.

Current state

0.1.0 is on CRAN, published 2026-10-16 from commit 1cc69d9 (the resubmission that named every zsv author in Authors@R). main is at 0.1.0.9000, with a # zucsv (development version) heading in NEWS.md; record every user-visible change under it. As of 2026-11-11 the 0.1.0 tag and its GitHub release have still not been created. The tag is the bare version, 0.1.0, not v0.1.0.

Versions and dependents

The next release is v0.1.1, tracked in #13: attach planned work to it as sub-issues. CRAN’s cadence opens on 2026-11-27, six weeks after publication (#14); that is the earliest a submission is allowed, not a plan to submit. Sibling packages that depend on this one: none recorded.

Any new vendored file that names an author means a new Authors@R entry: CRAN asked for every one by name.

Commands

Run from the package root. The everyday devtools loop is in .claude/shared/r-package.md; these are the package’s own.

R CMD INSTALL --preclean .              # when object files go stale
R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran zucsv_*.tar.gz
ZUCSV_STRESS=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'   # limits, millions of rows
Rscript bench/bench.R [reps]            # two-pass overhead vs read.csv()
tools/update-zsv.sh <commit-ish>        # re-vendor zsv, re-apply patches
Rscript tools/update-csv-spectrum.R     # regenerate test-spectrum.R
Rscript tools/check-csv-test-data.R     # csv-test-data conformance check

After editing C sources, devtools::load_all() recompiles; use R CMD INSTALL --preclean . when object files go stale.

Architecture

The design splits responsibility at one line (design §28):

zsv owns CSV syntax        →  where rows and fields begin and end
zucsv owns R semantics     →  NA matching, column types, data.frame
                              construction, error messages

Consequences that shape most implementation decisions:

  • Base R C API only, via .Call. No Rcpp, no cpp11, no runtime R package dependencies. Native symbols get registered in src/init.c with dynamic symbol lookup disabled; R/zucsv-package.R carries the @useDynLib zucsv, .registration = TRUE tag.
  • Thin R wrapper. read_csv() in R/read_csv.R normalizes arguments and calls one C routine.
  • Two passes over the file (design §9): pass 1 counts rows, fixes the column count, applies na matching, and infers types; pass 2 allocates each column at its exact final length and writes converted cells straight into it. No growable vectors, no intermediate row lists. This is why v0.1 accepts only seekable local file paths.
  • zsv is vendored, parser subset only, under src/vendor/zsv/ (see Vendored native code).

Exported names are unprefixed (zucsv::read_csv(), not zu_read_csv()): the package name is the namespace.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Validation that affects native safety is enforced in C, not only in the R wrapper.
  • Strict errors, never silent NA. A failed forced conversion, a ragged row, or an embedded NUL is an error carrying row, column, and column-name context. Raw zsv status codes stay internal.
  • Long jumps are the hazard. Every FILE *, zsv_parser, and native allocation must be released on R errors as well as on success (R_UnwindProtect() or an equivalent discipline), and the row loop calls R_CheckUserInterrupt() periodically (about every 16k rows), not per row.
  • Never build against a system zsv.
  • R-specific adaptation belongs in zucsv’s own src/ files, never in src/vendor/. The only changes to upstream are the patches in tools/patches/, applied by tools/update-zsv.sh.

Testing

  • Fixtures are raw bytes. helper-fixtures.R writes them with csv_file() and read_text(), so line endings, BOMs, NULs and invalid UTF-8 are exact and the test files stay pure ASCII.
  • test-spectrum.R is generated from csv-spectrum (BSD-2-Clause) by tools/update-csv-spectrum.R, as raw byte vectors so git cannot normalise the CRLF fixtures. Regenerate it; do not edit it by hand.
  • csv-test-data is not in the suite: it declares no licence, so tools/check-csv-test-data.R clones it at run time. Every fixture has a recorded expectation there, including the ones where zucsv deliberately differs, each with the design section that decides it.
  • test-upstream.R pins the vendored parser’s edge behaviour recorded in tools/zsv-behavior.md; it is what catches a change on re-vendoring.
  • test-differential.R compares with utils::read.csv() where the semantics overlap, with name repair off (zucsv does not repair names, design §5).
  • Stress tests are gated on ZUCSV_STRESS=true rather than skip_on_cran() (skip_unless_stress()): they check limits, not memory safety, and under gctorture they would cost hours.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-cmd-check.yml@v1: the GitHub runners plus the R-hub containers matching CRAN’s r-devel clang and GCC flavours, which see the bundled parser’s warnings before CRAN’s pretest does.
  • native-checks.yaml calls r-actions’ vendor.yml (a change under src/vendor must also change src/vendor/zsv/UPSTREAM, the manifest), sanitizers.yml (with asan: true), valgrind.yml (with --leak-check=full, so leaks on error and interrupt paths carry a stack), lto.yml, gctorture.yml, rchk.yml (fail-on-findings: true) and cran-special.yml (full only). It runs weekly on Tuesdays and on dispatch.
  • coverage.yaml calls coverage.yml@v1; pkgdown.yaml builds the site on pushes to main.

Deviations from .claude/shared/ci.md, as of 2026-11-11: no workflow calls changes.yml. native-checks.yaml skips prose-only changes with a paths-ignore list instead, and R-CMD-check.yaml deliberately has none, because README.md ships in the tarball and --as-cran checks its URLs. coverage.yaml is pinned to @v1, not to a commit. Bring these in line with ci.md in their own pull request.

Vendored native code

zsv from https://github.com/liquidaty/zsv, MIT, parser core only, at commit 61959542b18581e38f291957d9a500fab77be719 (v1.4.3-41-g6195954), vendored 2026-09-12. src/vendor/zsv/UPSTREAM records the upstream, commit, date, licence and the patches; tools/update-zsv.sh <commit-ish> re-vendors and rewrites it. src/vendor/zsv/src/zsv.c is a unity build, so src/Makevars lists vendor/zsv/src/zsv.o as the only vendored object. ZSV_EXTRAS is never defined, which keeps <sqlite3.h> and <zsv/utils/arg.h> out of the build.

Local patches, in tools/patches/:

  • 0001-guard-unused-forward-declaration.patch: keeps -Wunused-function clean.
  • 0002-no-stderr-default-sink.patch: removes the stderr/fprintf references so R CMD check’s compiled-code test passes.

After an upgrade, re-verify tools/zsv-behavior.md (what the parser does at the edges the design depends on: blank records, BOM, oversize rows, unbalanced quotes); tools/update-zsv.sh does not rewrite it.
